plainLanguage: The usual way of measuring chest-muscle activity with skin electrodes does not represent the whole muscle, and the measurement point effectively moves during a bench press.
qualifiers: This is a methodological finding, not a finding about training.
It applies to every tier-4 activation statement in this slice, including the ones drafted here.

conditions: surface electromyography over the pectoralis major during common shoulder tasks and the bench press

sourceLinks.locator: Title and Abstract (standard bipolar surface EMG estimations mischaracterise pectoralis major activity)
Title and Abstract (innervation-zone locations distribute medially during the bench press; offered as an explanation of conflicting activation reports)
Abstract, background (the bench press inclination literature is contradictory and measurement artefact is the likely reason)

statement: Standard bipolar surface electromyography mischaracterises pectoralis major activity in commonly performed tasks, and innervation-zone positions shift within the muscle during the bench press, so single-site surface EMG amplitude comparisons for this muscle are not reliably comparable.
